data.name: Amaryllis
data.gender_notes: Amaryllis is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Amaryllis was a nymph who loved Alcioneus, a shepherd. She was told to plant the beautiful red amaryllis flower in the ground and leave it undisturbed for 30 nights, after which it would bloom and reveal her love. Alcioneus, however, left for war and did not return. Amaryllis, in her despair, prayed for the flower to bloom in his absence, and it did, continuing to bloom every year on the anniversary of her love.
data.etymology: Amaryllis belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Jewel of the world.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Amaryllis total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_hebrew.name: אמריליס
in_hebrew.meaning: ענין לאמריליס הוא פרח נוי יפהפה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אמריליס הוא שם פרח שמקורו ביוונית, ומשמעותו קשורה לפרח הנוי יפהפה. אין אזכור ישיר לשם זה בתנ"ך, אך הפרח עצמו הוא סמל לטוהר ויופי. השם אמריליס משמש בעיקר במסגרת השמות הנוצריים, ומבטא את היופי והאור של הנצרות.

in_greek.name: Αμαρύλλης
in_greek.meaning: Το λουλούδι Amaryllis είναι ένα ωραίο λουλούδι
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Amaryllis προέρχεται από την ελληνική γλώσσα και σχετίζεται με το λουλούδι αμαρυλλίς, το οποίο είναι ένα σύμβολο ομορφιάς και αγνότητας. Στην παράδοση της Εκκλησίας, το λουλούδι αυτό αντιπροσωπεύει την πνευματική ομορφιά και την αγιότητα. Το όνομα Amaryllis χρησιμοποιείται στην παράδοση των χριστιανικών ονομάτων για να εκφράσει την πνευματική ανάπτυξη και την ομορφιά.

in_latin.name: Amaryllis
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Amaryllis a lingua Graeca derivatur et ad florem amaryllidis pertinet, qui est symbolum pulchritudinis et castitatis. In traditione ecclesiastica, flos hic repraesentat pulchritudinem spiritualem et sanctitatem. Nomen Amaryllis in traditione nominum christianorum adhibetur ad exprimendam incrementum spirituale et pulchritudinem.

The name Amaryllis is used to signify beauty, elegance, and refinement. It has been popularized in Christian cultures as a given name, reflecting the values of modesty, humility, and inner beauty.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Amaryllis represents new beginnings and divine beauty in Christian symbolism. Its name, derived from the Greek word for "majesty," underscores its association with the radiant beauty of Christ and the promise of a new life in faith.

historical_references.reference: According to Greek mythology, Amaryllis was a beautiful nymph who fell in love with the shepherd Alteo. To prove her love, she made a vow to the god Amor (Cupid) that she would remain chaste for one month, caring for a beautiful white lily that grew in her garden. At the end of the month, if the flower bloomed, she would marry Alteo. The flower did indeed bloom, and Amaryllis kept her vow by marrying Alteo. This legend probably dates back to ancient Greece.

The name Amaryllis has been associated with the Madonna lily, Lilium candidum, since the Middle Ages. In Christian symbolism, the white lily represents the Virgin Mary's purity and her perpetual virginity. The name Amaryllis may have been derived from the Greek name for this lily, 'amarysos', which means 'not deceiving'.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Amaryllis is derived from the ancient Greek word for 'sparkling'. In modern usage, Amaryllis is a popular name for a type of flower, which is often used in floral design for arrangements and events such as weddings. It is also used in home decor as a potted plant or as a scented candle. Amaryllis can be found on various social media and event planning platforms including Instagram, where it is frequently tagged in posts featuring floral arrangements and bouquets. It is also popular on Pinterest, where users create boards dedicated to Amaryllis flower decorations and DIY projects. Lastly, Amaryllis is a feature on many wedding websites, where it is used as a theme for various elements of the wedding, from the invitations to the table settings.
